reviewers.summary: The updated principal check blocks the previously reported indirect principal expressions. However, the ACR assignment filters still allow an additional AcrPush grant to the app identity when the role is specified without a literal Acr role_definition_name.

findingList.message: The AC RELEASE-ID-01 checks can miss an extra ACR grant when its role is specified by role_definition_id or a computed role name. Inspect all role assignments at the ACR and verify the app identity has no grant beyond AcrPull (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

evidence.codePathTraced: The ACR assignment checks only select resources whose role_definition_name is a literal beginning with "Acr". The new principal guard uses the same filter, so assignments using role_definition_id or a computed role name are skipped.
evidence.failureScenario: If an additional role assignment grants the app identity AcrPush on the ACR using role_definition_id, the assertions can still pass: the assignment is excluded from the counts and principal guard, leaving the app identity able to push images despite AC RELEASE-ID-01.

reviewers.summary: The latest guard catches indirect principal expressions when the role name is literal, but a local-based principal and role name can bypass the ACR grant checks.

findingList.message: AC RELEASE-ID-01 still permits an extra ACR grant when both the principal and role name use Terraform locals. Detect evaluated assignments or reject indirect role-name expressions.

evidence.codePathTraced: The ACR assignment checks recognize literal role names and direct identity or registry references. The app-grant count also requires direct references to the app identity and ACR.
evidence.failureScenario: If an extra ACR assignment uses principal_id = local.app_principal_id and role_definition_name = local.acr_push_role, with those locals resolving to the app identity and "AcrPush", the new guard skips it because its role name is not a literal "Acr...". The direct-reference count skips it too, so the test passes despite the app identity gaining push access.

reviewers.summary: The prior principal-expression bypasses are blocked for literal AcrPull/AcrPush role names. An assignment using locals for the role name and references can still evade the app grant checks.

findingList.message: The changed guard can miss an extra app ACR grant when the role name, principal, and scope are supplied through Terraform locals. Check evaluated assignments or reject indirect role-name expressions so this regression fails the test.

evidence.codePathTraced: The new guard examines only role assignments whose role_definition_name is written as a quoted literal beginning with Acr. The other app-grant count requires direct principal and scope references.
evidence.failureScenario: If an extra AcrPush assignment uses role_definition_name = local.push_role, principal_id = local.app_principal, and scope = local.acr_scope, with those locals resolving to AcrPush, the app identity, and the ACR, the literal-role guard skips it and the direct-reference count misses it. The test can pass while the app identity has push access, contrary to RELEASE-ID-01 (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).
